description:
Source rows that are the same flow as another row of the same list, shipped twice. Each entry names the duplicate and the row kept as valid, and says why that one. Both rows are still merged and must reach the same consensus flow -- a merge that sends them to two different flows stops, because the ruling says they are one. The duplicate's published mapping is marked `owl:deprecated`, with `dcterms:isReplacedBy` pointing at the valid row, and it does not count towards the match strength of the valid row's mapping: two copies of one flow are not two flows sharing a consensus flow. It is the source-list counterpart of `elementary-flow-collision-decisions.json`, which does the same for two flows this project publishes. A row names its list and not its release, as `land-flow-groupings.json` does. Read by `brightway_flows.merge.duplicate_rows`.

The first entries are GreenDelta's openLCA LCIA methods 2.8.2 package, which ships 181 land-use names twice, almost always once in `Resource / land` and once in `Resource / unspecified`; the `Resource / land` row is the valid one (decided 2026-10-13; 15 names whose class another name also reaches were added 2026-10-20, beside the fold in `land-flow-groupings.json`). It also ships 25 water names more than once, in `Resource / in water` and again in `Resource / unspecified`, `Resource / land` or `Resource / in ground`; there the `Resource / in water` row is the valid one (decided 2026-10-18, #389).
